analysis.title: Advance Auto Parts Inc. (AAP) 3Q26 Recap: Continued DIY softness amid macro pressures and execution. Commodity-related costs to be near-term margin headwind
key_insights: GS reiterates Sell on AAP after the 3Q26 print. Comparable sales missed, while adjusted EPS beat FactSet consensus. The stock traded down 5.2% against a 4.4% decline for the S&P 500.

GS expects AAP's margin recovery to take longer than expected, partly because of commodity-related margin headwinds in the near term. GS also views O'Reilly and AutoZone as better positioned to gain share.
AAP continues to lose share to auto parts retail peers despite a sequential comp improvement in 3Q. DIY comp kept declining.

DIFM comp was up low single digits, with positive performance in each month of the quarter. Main street customers outperformed by about 100bps on new customer acquisition and higher weekly spending tiers, helped by better parts availability and delivery times under 40 minutes.
National account portfolio optimization cut comp by 100bps in 3Q. GS expects it to remain a headwind through the rest of FY26 and into early 1Q27, to a lesser extent than in prior quarters.

DIY comp narrowed from worse than -4% in the first eight weeks of the quarter to a low single-digit decline in the final four weeks. GS attributes the decline to stretched household budgets, elevated energy costs and persistent inflation.

Higher oil costs raised product cost inflation. AAP's price increases did not fully offset it, so gross margin rate fell. Mix shift toward lower-margin categories such as motor oil cost about 20bps. Higher fuel costs, lower DIY mix and supply chain deleverage cost about 40bps.
Management expects 4Q gross margin below 3Q levels, and GS cuts its 4Q26 gross margin estimate to 44.4%. GS's FY26 gross margin estimate stays at 45.1%.

FY26 free cash flow guidance was raised to about $150mn, implying more than $400mn of y/y growth. Management credits stronger profitability and working capital discipline, including simpler sales collection and better vendor payables management. AAP is also lapping about $140mn of FY25 cash expenses tied to store optimization.
AAP expects FY26 capex of about $300mn. For FY27 it expects positive free cash flow and higher capex, with 4 new market hubs, new stores and in-store technology.
GS lowers FY26 EPS to $2.79 from $2.99, FY27 to $3.47 from $3.86 and FY28 to $4.50 from $4.96. It introduces FY29 EPS of $5.60. The FY27 and FY28 cuts reflect a lower sales outlook.

GS raises its 12-month price target to $43 from $40 despite the lower estimates. It lowers its market multiple to 18.5x from 22.5x but raises the downside/base/upside relative P/E multiples to 55%/60%/65%, citing less downside risk from structural and process improvements.

market_movers.rationale: Margin recovery is likely to take longer than expected, with oil-related cost pressure and continued share loss to ORLY and AZO. The price target rose to $43 from $40 on higher relative P/E multiples, which implies 15.3% downside from $50.75.

sector_views.stance: underweight AAP, with ORLY and AZO better positioned
sector_views.rationale: GS says AAP keeps losing share to peers while O'Reilly Auto Parts and AutoZone are better positioned to gain share in the current environment.

earnings_insights: AAP 3Q26 (reported 11/5/26): comparable sales missed, adjusted EPS beat FactSet consensus. The report gives no EPS figures for the quarter.
DIFM comp +LSD% in 3Q26, with main street customers about 100bps above the DIFM average. DIY comp was negative and narrowed to -LSD% in the final four weeks.
3Q26 gross margin pressure (reported): about 20bps from mix shift to lower-margin categories such as motor oil, about 40bps from higher fuel costs, lower DIY mix and supply chain deleverage.
Management guide: 4Q26 gross margin below 3Q26 levels. GS 4Q26E gross margin 44.4% (was 44.2%), GS FY26E gross margin 45.1% (unchanged).

GS estimate changes (GS forecasts, not consensus): 4Q26E EPS $0.20 (was $0.34), FY26E EPS $2.79 (was $2.99), FY27E $3.47 (was $3.86), FY28E $4.50 (was $4.96), FY29E $5.60 (new). 4Q26E operating income $37.7mn (was $50.4mn).
GS FY26E revenue $8,489.3mn (was $8,501.3mn), FY27E $8,654.1mn (was $8,707.7mn), FY28E $8,872.1mn (was $8,932.7mn). FY26E same-store sales growth 0.9%, FY27E 1.5%.
Company guidance: FY26 free cash flow about $150mn (raised), capex about $300mn. FY27 free cash flow expected positive, capex higher y/y, 4 market hubs planned.
GS risk/reward framework (GS forecasts): downside/base/upside implied price $19/$47/$57 at 25%/50%/25% probability, probability-weighted $43.

trade_ideas.description: Sell rating on AAP with a 12-month price target of $43.00, 15.3% below the $50.75 price
trade_ideas.rationale: Margin recovery is likely to take longer than expected and AAP continues to lose share to ORLY and AZO.
trade_ideas.risk: Better-than-expected same-store sales, faster expense reduction, progress on turnaround or supply chain initiatives, and deleveraging.

risk_factors: Better-than-expected same-store sales growth from DIFM share gains and a DIY recovery.
Faster-than-expected expense reduction leading to better margins and clearer line-of-sight to a sustainable margin recovery.
Substantial progress on turnaround initiatives that drive sales, or on supply chain initiatives that aid margins.
Deleveraging through operational improvements and debt reduction.
Oil and fuel cost inflation that prices cannot fully offset, which pressures gross margin (downside risk to AAP's margins).

tension_points.bull_case: Upside risks named by GS: better same-store sales from DIFM share gains and a DIY recovery, faster expense reduction, turnaround and supply chain progress, and deleveraging. GS also cites recent structural and process improvements that should drive more sustainable profitability.
tension_points.bear_case: GS argues margin recovery will take longer than expected. Oil-related costs cut gross margin in 3Q, AAP keeps losing share to ORLY and AZO, and DIY comp is still declining.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Better-than-expected same-store sales growth, or a faster-than-expected reduction in expenses that gives line-of-sight to a sustainable margin recovery.
